elements.element: No non-compete restriction imposed on Customer
elements.evidence: 12.4 ("Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor") is deleted in its entirety

elements.element: No field-of-use or territorial restriction on Customer's products/services
elements.evidence: remaining 12.3: "Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... or conducting business in any field or territory."

elements.element: No post-term survival of any compete restriction
elements.evidence: the "for twenty-four months thereafter" restriction no longer appears in the rendered clause

elements.element: Restriction limited to a named competing product
elements.evidence: no restriction remains; nothing names a competing product

elements.element: Restriction limited to the term only
elements.evidence: no restriction remains to be term-limited
no duration cap present because no restriction survives
no carve-out language; only the general 12.3 confirmation remains
no acquisition carve-out to a restriction, since no restriction exists

reasons: The single operation deletes paragraph 12.4, the only operative non-compete/field-of-use restriction on Customer, fully achieving the locked preferred level (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction).
Fallback elements are unmet only because no restriction survives at all; the preferred level is a stronger, self-contained bargain, so this is not a defect.

Minimality holds notwithstanding the mechanical whole-paragraph gate: paragraph 12.4 consists exclusively of the offending restriction, so no narrower edit (operator, number, or short phrase) would remove the prohibited non-compete.
Intent preserved: 12.3's affirmative confirmations remain effective, the internal contradiction between 12.3 and 12.4 is resolved, and no defined term, cross-reference, or mechanic is left dangling.
